claims.text: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances, which is exactly the measure POL-RD-22 prescribes: trip_record.actual_distance_km of 24.8 less trip_record.optimal_distance_km of 20.5 is 4.30 km, more than four times POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. POL-RD-22 expressly forbids re-measuring the route from the sparse trace, so the trace's low fix count cannot shrink this figure.

The driver never informed the rider of the deviation, as POL-RD-21 requires him to do by in-app chat before or at the point of deviation. None of the six chat entries announces a reroute or gives even a brief reason for one; the only messages sent while the trip ran are the rider's 13:24 query ('are we going the right way? This doesn't look like the usual route to the airport') and the driver's 13:25 reply 'Don't worry, I know the way. We will reach on time.', which explains nothing. Trip record's in_app_calls is empty, so no verbal notice can be established from the record (POL-GEN-26): the notice obligation is unmet and this is not an agreed deviation.

The excess distance fare is fixed by POL-RD-24's formula at the base per-km rate and without surge: 4.30 km x 0.80 SGD/km = 3.44 SGD. The fare ledger reports the same per_km_rate_sgd of 0.80 and the same excess_distance_fare_sgd of 3.44, matching the policy's own excess_distance_fare threshold block. That 3.44 SGD is the sum the rider is owed for the deviation.

Whichever open row of POL-RD-24's matrix applies, the rider is owed that 3.44 SGD in full: row (b) (traffic-justified but rider not informed) and row (d) (not traffic-justified) both pay the whole excess distance fare, so even accepting for argument that the PIE vehicle-fire advisory (EV-ADVIS-00902-01) satisfies POL-RD-23, that advisory can only move the case between rows (b) and (d) and cannot reduce the sum. Rows (a) and (c) are unavailable on this record: no notice was given, and 4.30 km is far outside the 1.0 km tolerance.

The only advisory anchored to the line the driver actually drove, the ECP one, does not justify a reroute under POL-RD-23: it does not intersect the recommended route and its type TRAFFIC_FLOW is not one of the kinds POL-RD-23 names (closure, congestion, incident). Whatever the driver believed about his alternative, his own route carries no admissible traffic justification of its own.

The rider is still carrying the charge. The ledger shows payment_status CHARGED, total_charged 35.00 and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so nothing has been returned to her. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION would leave that state standing and is not a rider-favourable outcome here; what the rider needs is a disposition that does not leave her bearing the disputed charge.

The AI cannot rule this case on its merits, and should not try: POL-RD-25 lets an AI ruling on a route deviation stand only where the deviation is 2 km or less, and this deviation is 4.30 km, so the case is escalated. That is the rider-protective disposition — under POL-GEN-03 an escalated case goes to a human reviewer, no monetary outcome issues and the contested amount is held rather than resolved against the rider — and it carries her 3.44 SGD excess-distance measure, and the balance of the 6.50 SGD she asks, to that reviewer instead of dismissing them.

The longer route was driven across the whole journey, not at its end: the trace's first fix is at 13:15:00 and its last at 13:52:00, the trip's own start and end, so the driver had the entire trip in which to give the POL-RD-21 notice and never did. The trace is IMPAIRED (issue LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, weight_multiplier 0.8) and I rely on its timestamps only; its geometry is not used to re-measure distance, exactly as POL-RD-22 directs.

Neither profile carries a fraud flag — rider 0 and driver 0 — so POL-GEN-22's 0.95 confidence uplift is not engaged, and the only obstacle between this record and an AI ruling is POL-RD-25's 2 km ceiling. The rider's claim is untarnished on the profile test that names this field and must not be dismissed on profile grounds.

The deviation the record establishes is 4.30 km — the trip record's own actual distance of 24.8 km less its recommended-route distance of 20.5 km — which is more than double the 2.0 km ceiling POL-RD-25 sets for an AI ruling. On that clause the AI cannot decide this case on its merits at all: it must go to a human reviewer, and under POL-GEN-03 an escalation is terminal, issues no monetary outcome and holds the amount, so the 35.00 SGD charged on this trip and the ledger's zero refund stay exactly as they are while that review runs. That is the order this record requires, and it is the order that leaves the driver's fare undisturbed.

The reroute was a response to real traffic on the recommended route, not the unexcused detour the rider alleges and not a route chosen for gain. LTA's advisory TC-001 records a vehicle fire on the PIE eastbound between Paya Lebar and Hougang, severity HIGH, lanes 1 and 2 blocked with long delays, active from 13:05 to 13:50 — the exact window in which this 13:15–13:52 trip ran — and TC-002 records heavy congestion on the PIE at the Changi Airport exit ramp over 13:15–13:40. Both intersect the recommended route, both overlap the trip window, and both are types POL-RD-23 admits (VEHICLE_FIRE and HEAVY_CONGESTION, each named in the clause's admissible list), so POL-RD-23's traffic-justification test is met and the driver's reroute falls inside the licence POL-RD-21 grants to reroute in response to real-time traffic and congestion.

Whatever the outcome, the money this case can move is not the 6.50 SGD the rider asks. POL-RD-24 measures the remedy as the deviation distance multiplied by the fare record's per-kilometre rate, without surge: 4.30 km x 0.80 SGD = 3.44 SGD. The fare ledger's own derived money block states the same figure at the same clause (excess_distance_fare_sgd 3.44, per_km_rate_sgd 0.80), so any refund on this trip is capped at 3.44 SGD and the rider's figure overstates the excess-distance fare by 3.06 SGD.

The 6.50 SGD the rider contests is the gap between the 28.50 SGD quoted fare and the 35.00 SGD meter total, not an excess-distance figure, and no row of POL-RD-24 returns a whole trip fare or a quote-versus-meter difference. Even the most the rider could reach on this record — row (b), a traffic-justified reroute with the rider not informed and a deviation over 1 km — pays only the excess distance fare, i.e. 3.44 SGD, and rows (c) and (e) pay nothing at all; under POL-GEN-03 no ruling value here returns the quote-to-meter gap, so the claim for the full 6.50 SGD is not one the policy provides.

The GPS trace is impaired, and I disclose it as such: issue code LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, weight_multiplier 0.80, 16 fixes at ~150 s intervals with 10 gaps exceeding the 120 s limb and a maximum gap of 210 s, and no fix carrying a reported horizontal accuracy. In any event POL-RD-22 forbids using the trace to re-measure the route, because a sparse trace understates a route's length, so the only admissible measure of the deviation is the trip record's own recorded distances — and they give 4.30 km, the very figure the rider pleads. The trace therefore neither enlarges nor reduces the distance at issue.
